newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea '96 GDP rises 7.1 pct vs 8.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea '96 GDP rises 7.1 pct vs 8.9 pct.

text.p: South Korea's gross domestic product (GDP) grew a real 7.1 percent in 1996 against an 8.9 percent rise a year earlier, provisional figures of the Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Thursday
NOTE - Figures in percentage and trillions of won.
Assistant BOK governor Kim Young-dae said the GDP was now expected to grow by about six percent this year, instead of an earlier forecast for a 6.4 percent gain.
"Conditions have worsened since we made our first forecast late last year," Kim said. "Strikes in January, the Hanbo collapse and the Sammi's failure all have negative impacts on the economy."

Weeks of strikes have cost the country $3.28 billion. Hanbo Steel Co, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, collapsed in January and the Sammi Group, the nation's 26th largest conglomerate, sought court receivership this week.
Kim said the economy appeared to have hit the bottom but there were no signs of a quick recovery.
He said better-than-expected rice harvest limited the slowdown in the GDP growth in 1996. The central bank had earlier projected a 6.9 percent growth for last year.
The central bank's figures showed private-sector consumption, investment and exports all slowed in 1996. The manufacturing and construction sectors's performance was poor.
Private consumption rose 6.9 percent last year, against an 8.3 percent rise in 1995.

Capital investment in 1996 rose 8.2 percent, compared with a gain of 15.8 percent in 1995, while construction investment increased 6.3 percent against an 8.7 percent rise, the central bank figures showed.
Exports rose 14.1 percent in 1996, down from a 24 percent rise a year before, while imports rose 14.8 percent against a 22.0 percent rise.
